nodes.name: IrO2 ink preparation A
nodes.procedure: A mass of 2.0 mg of IrO2 powder (iridium(IV) oxide, Premion, 99.99% (metal basis), ≥84.5% minimum, Alfa Aesar) was weighed into a pillbox. Volumes of 3.40 ml of ultra-pure water, then 1.70 ml of isopropyl alcohol (HPLC grade, Fisher Chemical) and finally 2.3 μl of 5 wt.% Nafion dispersion (1100EW, Sigma-Aldrich) were added to the pillbox. The synthesized ink was placed in an ultrasonic bath for homogenization.
nodes.source_text: IrO2 inks were prepared from IrO2 powder (iridium(IV) oxide, Premion, 99.99% (metal basis), ≥84.5% minimum, Alfa Aesar), 5 wt.% Nafion dispersion (1100EW, Sigma-Aldrich), isopropyl alcohol (high performance liquid chromatography, HPLC grade, Fisher Chemical) and ultra-pure water. Two inks were prepared with different loadings: 20 μg cm^-2 (ink A) and 100 μg cm^-2 (ink B). A mass of 2.0 mg (10 mg) of IrO2 powder was weighed into a pillbox for ink A (respectively for ink B).

nodes.name: IrO2 ink preparation B
nodes.procedure: A mass of 10 mg of IrO2 powder was weighed into a pillbox. Volumes of 3.39 ml of ultra-pure water, then 1.70 ml of isopropyl alcohol and finally 11.32 μl of Nafion dispersion were added to the pillbox. A content of 5 wt% Nafion and 95 wt% IrO2 was weighed, and a ratio of 1/3 isopropyl alcohol to 2/3 H2O was kept. The synthesized ink was placed in an ultrasonic bath for homogenization.

nodes.name: Carbon electrode preparation
nodes.procedure: A carbon electrode was polished to 1 μm, cleaned in an ultrasonic bath successively for 5 min each in acetone, ethanol and ultra-pure water and then placed in an oven at 90 °C for 20 min.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD showed different preferential grain orientations between wires and plates of Fe-Ni alloy catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Five alloys... were evaluated for the OER. XRD showed different preferential grain orientations between wires (labelled W) and plates (labelled P; Supplementary Fig. 1).

nodes.characterization_summary: GI-XRD shows fcc bulk structure for P-625 and P-825 with additional small wide peaks after activations identifying α-Ni(OH)₂ or NiFe LDH active surface layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both P-625 and P-825 have a face-centred cubic (fcc) bulk structure (determined by grazing incidence XRD (GI-XRD) after polishing; Fig. 2e). Additional small, wide peaks appear with the active-surface-layer formation.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM-EDS elemental profiles show Fe remains main component in W-316L active layer (Fe/Ni > 1) while other grades homogenize to 5-10 at% Fe and 15-20 at% Ni after activations.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to TEM-EDS elemental profiles (Fig. 3), although Fe remains the main component in the active surface layer of W-316L (Fe/Ni ratio > 1 after activations), ... the grades reach active-surface-layer compositions of 5–10 at.% Fe and 15–20 at.% Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM-ASTAR phase mapping shows bulk austenitic phase (red) and NiO cubic active surface layer (green); crystallographic orientation mapping reveals nanocrystallized structure with no preferential orientation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Phase mapping (Fig. 2h) highlights a bulk austenitic phase (red) and a NiO cubic active surface layer (green). ... ASTAR crystallographic orientation mapping using the same phases ... highlighting the nanocrystallized structure of the active surface layer with no preferential orientation.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ni 2p peaks at 852.6 eV (Ni⁰), 853.7 eV (NiO), 855.8 eV (Ni²⁺/Ni³⁺); Fe 2p peaks at 706.7 eV (Fe⁰), 710.7 eV (Fe₂O₃), 712.7 eV (FeOOH); Cr 2p at 573.6 eV (Cr⁰), 575.9 eV (Cr₂O₃), 577.2 eV (Cr(OH)₃).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 4 displays Ni 2p, Fe 2p and Cr 2p photoelectron lines of W-718 and W-625; ... The Ni 2p₃/₂ signal was deconvoluted to three main peaks at 852.6, 853.7 and 855.8 eV, attributed to Ni⁰, NiO and Ni²⁺/Ni³⁺, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM-EDS determines initial Fe content of alloys used for NiIII/NiII reduction peak potential correlation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Potential of NiIII/NiII reduction peak, extracted from Fig. 1a, as a function of the initial Fe content determined by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and EDS (Supplementary Table 1).
